input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (store name Zombie Match 3D, Harmony Games). Prepared by Julia Lawson, 1 Oct 2025.

This brief is written for the game as it is today. We are considering a change to the core gameplay; if the core changes, we will redo the affected parts of this brief with you in November.

1. Scenario and what it is for
We picked Scenario 1: the core gameplay, shown in its simplest, most authentic form. The goal is retention rather than the cheapest CPI: the playable should filter out players who won't like our game, while staying true to how the game actually plays. The player is not on rails: they pick items freely from the pile and can make several matches if they are good enough.

2. Start date
Kickoff and build start: Monday 3 November 2025 (kickoff call 9:00-9:30 am Pacific).

3. How a level plays
- Items sit in a 3D physics pile on the board. The player taps items to send them to a tray at the bottom.
- The tray has 7 slots. Three identical items in the tray match, clear, and are thrown at the zombies.
- If all 7 slots fill without a match, that is a blunder: the tray clears and the surviving zombies enrage, but play continues. A full tray is not a loss.
- Zombies walk toward the player. Different items have different abilities against them (e.g. grenade is powerful, couch does splash damage, plushies are weak but funny).
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach us and our HP runs out.

4. The board: eight items
The default board is these 8 items:
- Grenade
- Couch
- Plushie Chick
- Shuriken
- Cute Axe
- Gift Box
- Cactus Plant
- Dynamite
Every other board item on our pack list is an extra you can swap in on the platform (please keep the board items editable).

5. The zombies: four characters, one animation
- Characters: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player. All four are in the Unity package Marcus sent on 26 Sep.
- Animation: walk only. Please re-rig these four in Spine and carry over the walk animation only.
- The cannon in our pack is what you called the rocket launcher; it came with its projectile.

6. Reference level
Our reference level (built 23 Sep, recorded by Brian) used Grenade (red and green), Couch, Couch and Pillow, Plushie Bunny and Plushie Chick on the board, with a mix of zombies, and the same win and lose rules as above. The background in the first zip is the background of the reference level.

7. Sound and music
- You can use: Matching sound, Success sound, Failure sound. These are ours.
- Not yet: Rocket sound and Explosion sound. The current cues come from a sound library and a bought pack, so we can't hand them over; our own versions are still to be made, and we will send them when they exist.
- Background music: a new track made for the ad (not the in-game track). It is still being cut down to a loop and is still to come from us.
- Music starts only after the player's first tap/click, as per your rule from the Domino Delights playable.

8. Formats (as you told us; still holds)
- 3D: .fbx (exported in Binary, not ASCII), .glb or .blend
- 2D: .png (for 2D animation, character parts separated into pieces)
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

9. What is still coming from us
The hand-off list (Google Sheet, shared with you) has one row per item in our pack, with its state: Delivered (you have the current file), Ready (exported, current, waiting in our outgoing folder) or Owed (still being made or changed, with who has it). Check it to see what is still coming from us before 3 November.

Done. Brief and hand-off list are in my Drive, view-only for you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake.
• Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/0910494726922b6ec56f11f4/edit
• Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LpOvfLcZPy8LSzPX3LwGfvejGs9sDExFH0LGdFS_DHs/edit

Where the pack stands (96 lines):
• *Delivered: 8*
• *Ready: 56*
• *Owed: 32* (Claire 21, Brian 7, Calvin 3, Martin 1)

What changed from Brian's notes:
• Claire is redoing the bathroom UVs. The 12 bathroom FBXs she gave on Friday are the old version, so they go again.
• Robert made new colour versions of Cactus, Chainsaw and Cone on 29 Sep, after they were exported, so those go again too. Cactus is one of the eight on the board, so 7 of the 8 are Delivered or Ready and Cactus is still Owed.
• Calvin's sources sheet shows the Rocket sound comes from the Soundly library and the Explosion from a bought Unity pack. Both stay with us until Calvin makes our own versions. Matching, Success and Failure are ours and Ready.
The 32 Owed tickets under DES-313 are going to Todo, each with a comment. Delivered and Ready tickets are left as they are.

• *Brief* (what to build from: Scenario 1, the 8 board items, the 4 zombies + walk animation, win/lose and the 7-slot tray, sound and music): https://docs.google.com/document/d/0910494726922b6ec56f11f4/edit
• *Hand-off list* (every asset in our pack, marked Delivered / Ready / Owed, so you can see what's still coming from us): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LpOvfLcZPy8LSzPX3LwGfvejGs9sDExFH0LGdFS_DHs/edit
Both are shared with intake@playablex.ai too. The answer to your zombie question is in the brief: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician and Football Player, with the walk animation only. The brief is written for the game as it is today; if the core gameplay changes, we'll go through the affected parts with you in November.
